issues.description: The problem statement specifies that calculateTotalPrice(Meal) should return a double (UML and text: "double precision"), but the solution implementation declares calculateTotalPrice as returning an int. This is a return-type mismatch that affects the method signature students must implement and contradicts the stated precision requirement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the return type: update the method signature to return double in the implementation and in any templates/tests, and implement the calculation using double precision (e.g., change the return type to double and compute sum as double). Alternatively, if integer sums are intended, update the problem statement to require an int return type and remove references to "double precision".

issues.description: The problem statement instructs that SealSaloon should have a final Stock stock initialized in the constructor (instance field), but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across instances). The solution implements stock as a static final field. This is a structural contradiction in the specification about whether stock is an instance-final field initialized in the constructor or a static (class-level) field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify whether stock is intended to be shared across all SealSaloon instances (static) or instance-specific (final instance field). If stock should be shared, update the earlier instruction to remove initialization in the constructor and state that stock is static (initialize at declaration or in a static initializer). If stock should be an instance field, change the solution and any templates/tests to use a non-static final Stock initialized in the constructor.
